'''Trudy Frances Charlene Mackay''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born 10 September 1952)<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Mackay, Prof. Trudy Frances Charlene, (Mrs R. R. H. Anholt) | id = U151464 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.151464 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref> is the director of Clemson University's Center for Human Genetics<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://newsstand.clemson.edu/mediarelations/renowned-scientist-named-director-of-clemsons-center-for-human-genetics/|title=Renowned scientist named director of Clemson's Center for Human Genetics|website=Newsstand {{!}} Clemson University News and Stories, South Carolina|access-date=2018-08-24|archive-date=2020-09-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200907043109/https://newsstand.clemson.edu/mediarelations/renowned-scientist-named-director-of-clemsons-center-for-human-genetics/|url-status=dead}}</ref> located on the campus of the [[Greenwood, South Carolina|Greenwood]] Genetic Center.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ggc.org/|title=The Greenwood Genetic Center|website=www.ggc.org|language=en|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref> She is recognized as one of the world's leading authorities on the genetics of complex traits. Mackay is also the Self Family Chair in Human Genetics and Professor of Genetics and Biochemistry<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.clemson.edu/science/about/faculty-excellence.html|title=Salute to Faculty Excellence {{!}} College of Science, Clemson University, South Carolina|website=www.clemson.edu|access-date=2018-08-24|archive-date=2020-09-07|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200907043114/https://www.clemson.edu/science/about/faculty-excellence.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> at Clemson University.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.clemson.edu/|title=Clemson University, South Carolina|website=www.clemson.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref>

Mackay is a member of the National Academy of Sciences (2010).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nasonline.org/directory-entry/trudy-f-c-mackay-i0rg3f/|title=Trudy Mackay|website=www.nasonline.org|access-date=2018-08-24}}</ref>

Mackay was formerly the [[William Neal Reynolds]] and Distinguished University Professor at [[North Carolina State University]],<ref>{{cite web | title = Mackay Homepage | publisher = 
| date = | url = http://www.cals.ncsu.edu/genetics/mackay/mackay.html
| accessdate = 2008-07-21 |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20080423150456/http://www.cals.ncsu.edu/genetics/mackay/mackay.html <!-- Bot retrieved archive --> |archivedate = 2008-04-23}} Faculty webpage</ref><ref name="Mackay2006">{{cite journal|last1=Mackay|first1=Trudy|title=Trudy Mackay|journal=[[Current Biology]]|volume=16|issue=17|year=2006|pages=R659–R661|issn=0960-9822|doi=10.1016/j.cub.2006.08.016|pmid=16991214|doi-access=free}} {{free access}}</ref><ref name="youtube">{{cite web|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FXF_6T6BzqY |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/FXF_6T6BzqY |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live|website=youtube.com|publisher=[[YouTube]]|title=NC State: Trudy Mackay}}{{cbignore}}</ref> where she specialized in [[quantitative genetics]].<ref name="MackayStone2009">{{cite journal|last1=Mackay|first1=Trudy F. ==Education==
Mackay received a [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1974 and [[Master of Science]] degree in 1976 in Biology from [[Dalhousie University]].<ref name=whoswho/> She completed postgraduate study at the [[University of Edinburgh]] with a [[PhD]] in [[genetics]] awarded in 1979 for research supervised by [[Alan Robertson (geneticist)|Alan Robertson]].<ref name=truphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Edinburgh|hdl=1842/11082|title=Genetic variation in varying environments|first= Trudy Frances Charlene |last=Mackay|date=1979|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.502971}}|oclc=757072704}} {{free access}}</ref><ref name=cv>{{cite web|url=https://mackay.gnets.ncsu.edu/files/2015/08/CV_Mackay_06_2015_for-Website.pdf|title=Trudy Mackay CV|website=mackay.gnets.ncsu.edu}}{{Dead link|date=September 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref>

==Career and research==
Mackay's research investigates the environmental and genetic factors that influence [[quantitative trait]]s.<ref name=frs/> These [[phenotypic trait]]s include height or weight and are represented by [[Continuous or discrete variable|continuous, rather than discrete, values]].<ref name=frs/> Her work is undertaken by studying the impact of natural variants and [[mutation]]s on many behavioural, morphological, physiological and life history traits in [[Drosophilidae|fruit flies]], which she uses as a [[model organism]].<ref name=frs/>

The broad importance of such traits gives Mackay's work potential application in many areas — from improving [[plant breeding]] and [[animal breeding]] to the treatment of [[Disease|human disease]]s.<ref name=frs/> Mackay is the co-author with [[Douglas Scott Falconer]] of the fourth edition of the widely used and highly cited textbook, ''Introduction to Quantitative Genetics'', published in 1996.<ref name=iqg>{{Cite book|url=https://archive.org/details/introductiontoqu00falc|title=Introduction to quantitative genetics|last1=Falconer|first1=Douglas|date=1996|publisher=Longman|last2=Mackay|first2=Trudy F. C.|isbn=9780582243026|edition=4th|location=Essex, England|oclc=34415160|url-access=registration}}</ref>

===Awards and honours===
Mackay was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS) in 2006.<ref name=frs>{{cite web|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151117111158/https://royalsociety.org/people/trudy-mackay-11854/|archivedate=2015-11-17|url=https://royalsociety.org/people/trudy-mackay-11854/|website=royalsociety.org|publisher=[[Royal Society]]|location=London|author=Anon|year=2006|title=Professor Trudy Mackay FRS}} One or more of the preceding sentences incorporates text from the royalsociety.org website where: {{quote|“All text published under the heading 'Biography' on Fellow profile pages is available under [[Creative Commons license|Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License]].” --{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |title=Royal Society Terms, conditions and policies |accessdate=2016-03-09 |url-status=bot: unknown |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20161111170346/https://royalsociety.org/about-us/terms-conditions-policies/ |archivedate=2016-11-11 }}}}</ref>  She was awarded the [[Genetics Society of America Medal]] in 2004<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Weir|first=Bruce|date=2004|title=The 2004 Genetics Society of America Medal Trudy F. C. Mackay|journal=Genetics|volume=166|issue=2|pages=647–648|doi=10.1534/genetics.166.2.647|pmid=15020454|pmc=1470721}}</ref> and the [[Wolf Prize in Agriculture]] in 2016.<ref name=TarHeel>{{cite news|last1=Maguire|first1=Marti|title=Tar Heel: Trudy Mackay works with fruit flies to solve genetic mysteries|url=http://www.newsobserver.com/news/local/counties/wake-county/article58863923.html|accessdate=16 February 2016|publisher=The News & Observer|date=February 6, 2016}}</ref> She was elected to the [[American Philosophical Society]] in 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=The American Philosophical Society Welcomes New Members for 2021|url=https://www.amphilsoc.org/blog/american-philosophical-society-welcomes-new-members-2021|access-date=2021-05-12|website=American Philosophical Society|language=en}}</ref> She is a recipient of [[Trinity College Dublin|Trinity College]]’s Dawson Prize in Genetics in 2018.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Ground-breaking geneticist, Trudy Mackay, to receive prestigious Dawson Prize|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2018-10/tcd-ggt103118.php|access-date=2021-05-12|website=EurekAlert!|language=en}}</ref> She was elected [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]] in 2003.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Fellows of AAAS|url=https://www.aaas.org/sites/default/files/AnnualReports/2003/20-fellows.pdf}}</ref> She became a member of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2005.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Trudy F.C. Mackay|url=https://www.amacad.org/person/trudy-fc-mackay|access-date=2021-05-12|website=American Academy of Arts & Sciences|language=en}}</ref> Mackay was elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Medicine]] in 2024,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-10-21 |title=National Academy of Medicine Elects 100 New Members |url=https://nam.edu/news-and-insights/national-academy-of-medicine-elects-100-new-members-6/ |access-date=2025-03-28 |website=National Academy of Medicine}}</ref> and was awarded the [[Darwin–Wallace Medal]] in 2025.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Announcing the Linnean Society's Medal and Award Recipients 2025 |url=https://www.linnean.org/news/2025/04/09/announcing-the-linnean-societys-medal-and-award-recipients-2025 |access-date=2025-04-09 |website=The Linnean Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Mackay married Robert R. H. Anholt in 1990.<ref name=whoswho/>
